sentences.text: The appellant / Insurance Company, aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, III Additional District Judge, Dharapuram, in M.C.O.P.No.338 of 2011, dated 14.06.2016, has filed the present appeal.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, III Additional District Judge, Dharapuram
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal.
3. The facts required for the disposal of the appeal is that on 21.06.2010 at about 4.00 a.m, the deceased Manokaran was driving the car bearing Registration No.TN-07-W-9510 towards Thennilai.
When the car proceeding towards Coimbatore to Karur Main Road near Nallipalayam, at that time, the deceased lost control of the car and dashed against the lorry coming in the opposite direction.
As a result of which, the front portion of the car was entirely damaged and the deceased Manokaran was sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot itself.

It was alleged in the claim _________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis petition that the deceased was aged about 38 years at the time of the accident and was earning Rs.7,500/- per month as driver of the first respondent,
who was the owner of the car.
Claiming compensation of Rs.11,00,000/-, the wife of the deceased filed the claim petition.

4. The Insurance Company has filed the counter affidavit before the Tribunal stating that the deceased was not working as a driver with the first respondent and that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the deceased which is a violation of the policy conditions.
It was also stated that the deceased was the owner of the vehicle and that he had purchased the vehicle from the first respondent and was driving the vehicle without making changes in the RC Book.
That apart, it was stated that there was no documentary evidence to prove the age, income and avocation of the deceased.
Therefore, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal was excessive and that the same needs interference of this Court.
_ _ _ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

5. The Insurance Company filed additional counter affidavit stating that the Insurance Company was wrongly added as a party in the claim petition and that owner of the offending vehicle was not impleaded and therefore, the claim petition has to fail for non-joinder of necessary parties.
6. There is no representation for the respondent herein.

7. The Tribunal on considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the documents placed on record, came to the conclusion that since the offending vehicle was not traceble by the Police, it was concluded that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the deceased.

With respect to the violation of the policy conditions, the Tribunal came to the conclusion that since the Insurance Company itself has conceded that the deceased was not working as driver with the first respondent and that he had purchased the vehicle from the first respondent, the compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- was payable to the owner of the vehicle by the Insurance _________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Company.

Finally, the Tribunal came to the conclusion that though the policy was in the name of the third party but since the policy was in vogue as on the date of the accident, the Insurance Company was liable to pay a compensation of Rs.2,00,000/-.
Accordingly, the Tribunal allowed the claim petition.
Questioning the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the appellant / Insurance Company has filed the appeal.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is seen from the records that the first respondent is the owner of the vehicle involved in the accident and the said vehicle was covered under Personal Accident Coverage Policy.

As per the Judgment of this Court in Royal Sundaram Allianz Insurance Company, if the vehicle is covered under the Personal Accident Coverage Policy for Owner / Driver, the insurer shall undertake to pay compensation.
In the instant case, the deceased is not a third party and he is also not the owner/driver of the vehicle and he was also not an employee of the first respondent.

However, the Tribunal, has granted a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- under the Personal Accident Coverage Policy for o w n e r / d r i v e r s i n c e t h e i n s u r a n c e p o l i c y w a s i n e x i s t e n c e .
_ _ _ _ _ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 9.

In the aforestated circumstances, this Court is of the view that as per the judgment (supra) of this Court, compensation payable under the Personal Accident Coverage Policy is applicable only for owner-cum-driver.

In the instant case, though it is the claim of the wife of the deceased that the deceased had purchased the vehicle, it is seen from records that no steps have been taken to transfer the vehicle in the name of the deceased and as on today, it stands in the name of the first respondent.
Hence, viewing from any angle, there is no proof to establish that the deceased was the owner of the vehicle.
In such circumstances, the grant of compensation under the Personal Accident Coverage Policy for Owner / Driver is unsustainable.
10. For the aforestated reasons, the award passed by the Tribunal is liable to be set aside.

Accordingly, the judgment and decree dated 14.06.2016 made in M.C.O.P.No.338 of 2011 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, III Additional District Judge, Dharapuram, is set aside and the Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is allowed.
